👉 What?
➡️ The European Union has officially approved the AI Act, marking the world’s first major legislative effort to regulate artificial intelligence

👉 How does it work?
➡️ The AI Act applies a risk-based approach, meaning different AI applications are regulated based on their perceived risks to society

➡️ AI applications deemed “unacceptable” are banned outright:  These include "social scoring" systems that rank citizens based on aggregation and analysis of their data, predictive policing and emotional recognition in the workplace and schools

➡️ High-risk systems, including autonomous vehicles, medical devices, financial services, and educational tools, will be closely scrutinised for health, safety, and fundamental rights risks

➡️ “With the AI act, Europe emphasises the importance of trust, transparency and accountability when dealing with new technologies while at the same time ensuring this fast-changing technology can flourish and boost European innovation,” says Mathieu Michel, Belgium's secretary of state for digitisation said in a Tuesday statement

👉 Penalty
➡️ Companies in violation of the AI Act can face fines ranging from €7 million ($8.2 million) to €35 million ($38 million) or 7% of their annual global revenue, whichever is higher

👉 Impact on generative AI systems like ChatGPT
➡️ The Act places tough restrictions on generative AI systems, requiring adherence to EU copyright laws, transparency in model training, routine testing, and cybersecurity protections

➡️ These restrictions will begin 12 months after the law comes into force, with a 36-month transition period for existing AI systems like ChatGPT, Google’s Gemini, and Microsoft’s Copilot to achieve compliance

Source: CNBC

EU AI Act - the World's first regulation on Artificial Intelligence comes into force tomorrow (1 August, 2024) - here are 7 things you need to know based on my research so far no matter where you are in the world👇🏾

1️⃣ Who does the "EU AI Act" apply to?
- Legal framework applies to public & private actors inside and outside EU, if the "AI system" is placed on the Union market or it's use affects people located in EU.

2️⃣ Risk Levels for AI Systems
- Unacceptable Risk, High Risk, Limited risk & low or minimal risk.
Simple words - Unacceptable Risk would be something shown in some Black Mirror episodes that are used to trigger change in behaviour of humans e.g exploiting vulnerable people, biometrics identification in public space etc  High Risk would be systems in products like Aviation systems, cars, medical devices  lifts etc

3️⃣ Is there a Regulator for "EU AI Act" in EU?
- "European Artificial Intelligence Board" which will have the "National competent authorities", a combination of EU Member States designated authority & at least 1 market surveillance authority.

4️⃣  Does the US have one of these Regulator?
- As of 1 August, 2024 - there is currently no federal legislation in the US that directly regulates AI.

5️⃣  Does the UK have one of these Regulators?
- As of 1 August, 2024 - there is currently no Central AI regulator or any existing plans to establish one either as per their whitepaper

6️⃣  Does the UK have one of these Regulators?
- As of 1 August, 2024 - there is currently no Central AI regulator

7️⃣  There are many parts to this and i would recommend reading the FAQ from the EU AI Act - they have been very comprehensive.

Note 1- Even though the Act is coming into force on 1 August, 2024, it will only be effective from 2 August, 2026 (with some exceptions)
